The Test Center would like to lease back some or all of these tracts from the Panamanian Government at a reasonable rental. It is having some problems trying to establish what a fair rental value would be as there have been no market values for leases of comparable lands in the Zone. The Center has also been exploring other alternatives in case a reasonable rental cannot be worked out.
RENARE, the Panamanian agency responsible for national parks, would like to see this area preserved and would favor the Test Center lease arrangement or designation of the tract as a park.
A third alternative, of course, if both of these arrangements should fail, would be for the area to be deforested through slash and burn practices by squatters or commercial timbering.
-- The Fort Sherman-San Larenzo-Achiote Road area is forested and rich in birdlife. Under the new Canal Treaty, Fort Sherman cantonment and the area along highway S-2 will be a U.S. defense site, while the adjoining Fort Sherman training area will become a joint area of military coordination in which U.S. standards of fire prevention, safety and sanitation will apply.
While these actions will provide protection to a number of tracts of interest to environmental groups, there will be large areas (about 2/3rds of the Canal Zone area) in which environmental protection will depend on Panamanian legislation and enforcement. Panamanian forestry, water, hunting and fishing laws and regulations appear to provide an adequate legal base for such protection. The Joint Environmental Commission provided for by the Treaty should also give the U.S. influence in this area. In addition, Panama is a party to the 1940 Convention on Nature Protection and Wild Life Preservation in the Western Hemisphere.
